detections.evidence_quote: looking at someone's blood, can you get a sense of how long until they're going to die?
detections.summary: Interviewer asks whether blood tests can tell how long someone will live or measure longevity.

detections.evidence_quote: what you're not going to get on a standard blood test is any of the longevity genes.
detections.summary: Attia says standard blood tests do not show longevity genes, naming APOE and Lp(a) as longevity genes.

detections.evidence_quote: So the lower your LP little A, the greater your chance of cardiovascular mortality.
detections.summary: Attia links Lp(a) levels to cardiovascular mortality risk.

detections.evidence_quote: what is this person's risk of atherosclerotic disease, so heart disease or stroke?
detections.summary: Attia frames longevity blood work as assessing risk of atherosclerotic disease (heart disease, stroke), cancer and neurodegenerative disease.

detections.evidence_quote: Cardiovascular disease largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction.
detections.summary: Attia says cardiovascular disease is driven by lipoproteins, inflammation and endothelial dysfunction and lists the lipoprotein markers (Lp(a), LDL particle number, small LDL, VLDL) blood can show.

detections.evidence_quote: we can see things like fibrinogen, C-reactive protein.
detections.summary: Attia lists non-specific (fibrinogen, CRP) and specific (ox-LDL, Lp-PLA2, oxidized phospholipid) inflammation markers measurable in blood.

detections.evidence_quote: I think that insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium.
detections.summary: Attia says endothelial health is hardest to measure, counts insulin as toxic to the endothelium at high levels, and lists homocysteine, ADMA and SDMA as markers.

detections.evidence_quote: looked at cardiovascular health in patients with type 1 diabetes
detections.summary: Attia mentions a James O'Keefe paper using insulin doses in type 1 diabetes patients to assess cardiovascular impact.

detections.evidence_quote: The older a patient gets, the more I would probably rely on things like CT angiograms
detections.summary: Attia says blood tells most of a younger person's cardiovascular risk, older patients need CT angiograms, and a low calcium score is weakly reassuring because half of events occur at non-calcified lesions.

detections.evidence_quote: until companies like GRAIL have fully functioning liquid biopsies
detections.summary: Attia says blood gives the least insight into cancer risk until liquid biopsies like GRAIL's fully work.

detections.evidence_quote: virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
detections.summary: Attia says nearly all cancers come from somatic rather than germline mutations, so genotyping helps little apart from BRCA or Lynch.

detections.evidence_quote: for me, minimizing hyperinsulinemia becomes very important
detections.summary: Attia says cancer risk assessment comes down to inflammation and metabolic health, making minimizing hyperinsulinemia important.

detections.evidence_quote: James O'Keefe just recently was on a paper that looked at cardiovascular health in patients with type 1 diabetes
detections.summary: Attia cites a recent paper by James O'Keefe on insulin doses and cardiovascular health in type 1 diabetics.

detections.evidence_quote: based on a study in one of the atherosclerosis journals, was you know looking at fifty percent of patients that had that had events
detections.summary: Attia cites a recent editorial on an atherosclerosis-journal study finding half of events occurred at non-calcified lesions.

detections.evidence_quote: I include insulin here because I think that insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium.
detections.summary: Insulin's toxicity to the endothelium is offered as the reason to measure insulin for cardiovascular risk.

detections.evidence_quote: So, knowing your genotype doesn't really help, outside of a few outlier things like BRCA or Lynch.
detections.summary: The somatic origin of cancer mutations is offered to explain why genotype testing helps little.

product_mentions.evidence_quote: until companies like GRAIL have fully functioning liquid biopsies

verification_candidates.claim_text: APOE is one of the longevity genes.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: you certainly APOE would be one of the longevity genes.
verification_candidates.rationale: Genetic claim about lifespan determinants that could be checked.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The lower a person's Lp(a), the greater their chance of cardiovascular mortality.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: So the lower your LP little A, the greater your chance of cardiovascular mortality.
verification_candidates.rationale: Direction of the Lp(a)-mortality relationship as stated is checkable and may be misspoken.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Cardiovascular disease is largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Cardiovascular disease largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction.
verification_candidates.rationale: Causal model of heart disease that shapes what listeners test for.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Insulin is itself toxic to the endothelium at high levels.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I think that insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium.
verification_candidates.rationale: Causal claim about insulin damaging blood vessels.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) and SDMA are inhibitors of nitric oxide synthase.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: asymmetric dimethylarginine, or ADMA, and SDMA, which are inhibitors of nitric oxide synthase.
verification_candidates.rationale: Biochemical mechanism offered to justify a cardiovascular marker.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The younger a person is, the more blood tests reveal about cardiovascular risk; for a typical 40-year-old, blood tests give about 80 to 85 percent of what is needed to know.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the younger you are, the more your blood tells me about your risk of cardiovascular disease.
verification_candidates.rationale: Quantified claim about the diagnostic value of blood tests for heart risk.

verification_candidates.claim_text: By the time patients are older a calcium score usually becomes less relevant, though it can be somewhat helpful in a younger patient.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: usually by the time they're older, a calcium score becomes less relevant.
verification_candidates.rationale: Claim about when a cardiac screening test is informative.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A recent study found that fifty percent of patients who had cardiac events had them at the site of non-calcified lesions, so a low calcium score is not very reassuring.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: looking at fifty percent of patients that had that had events had them at the site. Of non-calcified lesions
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific study finding that bears on trust in calcium scoring.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Blood tests give the least insight into cancer risk compared with cardiovascular and other disease risk.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: On the cancer side, I think that's really, frankly, where blood gives us the least insight.
verification_candidates.rationale: Claim about the diagnostic limits of blood testing for cancer.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
verification_candidates.rationale: Broad causal claim about cancer origins.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Knowing one's genotype does not help assess cancer risk, apart from a few outliers such as BRCA or Lynch syndrome.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: knowing your genotype doesn't really help, outside of a few outlier things like BRCA or Lynch.
verification_candidates.rationale: Bears on whether listeners pursue genetic testing for cancer risk.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Cancer risk comes down to inflammation and metabolic health, so minimizing hyperinsulinemia is important for reducing it.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: in cancer, it really comes down to understanding inflammation, which we've already addressed, and metabolic health
verification_candidates.rationale: Implies hyperinsulinemia and inflammation drive cancer risk.
